nodes.summary: Introduces ACC-Collab, a training framework that teaches a two-agent actor-critic LLM team to collaborate through guided trajectories and preference optimization, outperforming multi-agent debate and fine-tuning baselines on several QA benchmarks.
nodes.title: ACC-Collab: An Actor-Critic Approach to Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration

nodes.summary: Argues that AI agent benchmarks need cost-controlled comparisons, shortcut-resistant holdouts, downstream-relevant metrics, and standardized evaluation to measure real-world usefulness rather than leaderboard accuracy alone.
nodes.title: AI Agents That Matter

nodes.summary: Introduces a Gemini 2.0-based multi-agent AI co-scientist for scientist-in-the-loop hypothesis generation, with automated and expert evaluations plus preliminary biomedical validations in drug repurposing, liver fibrosis, and antimicrobial resistance.
nodes.title: Towards an AI co-scientist

nodes.summary: Introduces The AI Scientist, an end-to-end LLM agent pipeline that generates ML research ideas, implements experiments, writes papers, and uses automated review to evaluate generated discoveries.
nodes.title: The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery

nodes.summary: Evaluates scientific LLM agents with Corral and argues that current agents can complete workflows while failing to exhibit evidence-sensitive scientific reasoning.
nodes.title: AI scientists produce results without reasoning scientifically

nodes.summary: Introduces A-Mem, a Zettelkasten-inspired agentic memory system that constructs, links, evolves, and retrieves structured notes for LLM agents in long-term conversational tasks.
nodes.title: A-Mem: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents

nodes.summary: Introduces AgentBench, an eight-environment benchmark and toolkit for evaluating LLMs as interactive agents across code, game, and web-grounded tasks.
nodes.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents

nodes.summary: Introduces AgentBoard, a benchmark and open-source analytical evaluation framework for multi-turn LLM agents across diverse text-based, partially observable environments with fine-grained progress metrics.
nodes.title: AgentBoard: An Analytical Evaluation Board of Multi-turn LLM Agents

nodes.summary: Introduces a three-agent code-generation framework that separates programming, test design, and local test execution to iteratively repair LLM-generated code on HumanEval and MBPP-style benchmarks.
nodes.title: AgentCoder: Multi-Agent Code Generation with Effective Testing and Self-optimisation

nodes.summary: Introduces Agent Hospital and MedAgent-Zero, a synthetic hospital simulacrum where LLM doctor agents learn from generated patient cases and validated reflections, with reported gains on virtual medical tasks and MedQA.
nodes.title: Agent Hospital: A Simulacrum of Hospital with Evolvable Medical Agents

nodes.summary: Introduces Agent Laboratory, an open-source LLM-agent research assistant that turns a human research idea into a literature review, ML experiments, code, and a report, with evaluations of autonomous and human-guided operation.
nodes.title: Agent Laboratory: Using LLM Agents as Research Assistants

nodes.summary: Introduces AgentNet, a decentralized LLM multi-agent framework where agents route tasks over an evolving DAG and refine local expertise through retrieval-augmented trajectory memories.
nodes.title: AgentNet: Decentralized Evolutionary Coordination for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems

nodes.summary: Introduces AgentRxiv, a shared preprint-server framework that lets autonomous research agents upload, retrieve, and build on prior agent-generated papers for cumulative and parallel scientific discovery.
nodes.title: AgentRxiv: Towards Collaborative Autonomous Research

nodes.summary: Explains diminishing returns in LLM multi-agent scaling through effective information channels and shows that heterogeneous agents can outperform much larger homogeneous ensembles.
nodes.title: Understanding Agent Scaling in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems via Diversity

nodes.summary: Introduces AgentScope, a developer-centric platform for LLM multi-agent applications with message-based workflow programming, fault tolerance, tool/RAG/multimodal support, and actor-based distributed deployment.
nodes.title: AgentScope: A Flexible yet Robust Multi-Agent Platform

nodes.summary: Introduces AgentVerse, a four-stage LLM multi-agent framework for dynamic expert recruitment, collaborative decision-making, execution, and evaluation across reasoning, coding, tool-use, and embodied-agent tasks.
nodes.title: AgentVerse: Facilitating Multi-Agent Collaboration and Exploring Emergent Behaviors

nodes.summary: Introduces Agentless, a non-agentic SWE-bench issue-resolution pipeline using staged localization, Search/Replace patch sampling, and regression plus reproduction-test selection as a strong simple baseline for software engineering agents.
nodes.title: Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents

nodes.summary: Introduces AgentsNet, a scalable benchmark that tests whether LLM agent networks can coordinate through local message passing on graph-theoretic distributed computing tasks.
nodes.title: AgentsNet: Coordination and Collaborative Reasoning in Multi-Agent LLMs

nodes.summary: Introduces AndroidWorld, an ICLR 2025 benchmark environment with dynamic Android app tasks and device-state rewards for evaluating autonomous computer-control agents.
nodes.title: AndroidWorld: A Dynamic Benchmarking Environment for Autonomous Agents

nodes.summary: Presents a zero-code LLM agent framework that turns natural-language requirements into tools, agents, and workflows and evaluates the resulting generalist stack on GAIA, MultiHop-RAG, and open-ended creation tasks.
nodes.title: AutoAgent: A Fully-Automated and Zero-Code Framework for LLM Agents

nodes.summary: Introduces AutoAgents, a framework that dynamically builds task-specific LLM agent teams, plans their collaboration, and uses observer-guided refinement to improve multi-agent task solving.
nodes.title: AutoAgents: A Framework for Automatic Agent Generation

nodes.summary: Introduces AutoGen, an open-source framework for building LLM applications as programmable conversations among customizable agents that can use LLMs, tools, code execution, and human input.
nodes.title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation

nodes.summary: Introduces the BrowserGym and AgentLab ecosystem for unified web-agent benchmark integration, reproducible large-scale experiments, and cross-model evaluation of browser-using LLM agents.
nodes.title: The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research

nodes.summary: Introduces CAID, a branch-and-merge multi-agent coordination pattern for long-horizon software engineering tasks using centralized delegation, isolated worktrees, and test-based integration.
nodes.title: Effective Strategies for Asynchronous Software Engineering Agents

nodes.summary: Introduces CAMEL, a role-playing framework for autonomous LLM agent cooperation that generated AI Society, Code, Math, and Science instruction datasets and exposed practical failure modes in communicative agents.
nodes.title: CAMEL: Communicative Agents for \"Mind\" Exploration of Large Language Model Society

nodes.summary: Introduces COMA, a centralized-critic decentralized-actor policy-gradient method with a counterfactual baseline for multi-agent credit assignment in cooperative reinforcement learning.
nodes.title: Counterfactual Multi-Agent Policy Gradients

nodes.summary: Introduces ChatDev, a role-based multi-agent LLM framework that turns software requirements into prototype code through chat-chain coordination across design, coding, review, and testing.
nodes.title: ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development

nodes.summary: Introduces ChatEval, a multi-agent debate framework that uses role-diverse LLM referees and communication strategies to improve alignment with human text-evaluation judgments.
nodes.title: ChatEval: Towards Better LLM-based Evaluators through Multi-Agent Debate

nodes.summary: Introduces Collab-Overcooked, a forced-collaboration Overcooked-AI benchmark with process metrics for evaluating how LLM agents initiate and respond to collaboration.
nodes.title: Collab-Overcooked: Benchmarking and Evaluating Large Language Models as Collaborative Agents

nodes.summary: Introduces CommNet, a differentiable continuous-communication architecture for cooperative multi-agent tasks, and demonstrates learned communication on lever-pulling, traffic, combat, and bAbI settings.
nodes.title: Learning Multiagent Communication with Backpropagation

nodes.summary: CooperBench evaluates collaborative coding agents and finds that two-agent cooperation often underperforms a solo agent because communication and coordination fail under partial observability.
nodes.title: CooperBench: Why Coding Agents Cannot be Your Teammates Yet

nodes.summary: Introduces Curie, an AI-agent framework and benchmark for rigorous automated experimentation through validation, controlled agent coordination, and structured experiment knowledge.
nodes.title: Curie: Toward Rigorous and Automated Scientific Experimentation with AI Agents

nodes.summary: DELEGATE-52 evaluates long-horizon delegated document editing across 52 domains and finds that current LLMs accumulate sparse but severe content corruption.
nodes.title: LLMs Corrupt Your Documents When You Delegate

nodes.summary: Documents OpenAI Five, a large-scale self-play reinforcement-learning system that reached superhuman Dota 2 play while exposing practical lessons about scaling, data freshness, long horizons, and continual training across a changing environment.
nodes.title: Dota 2 with Large Scale Deep Reinforcement Learning

nodes.summary: Introduces DyLAN, a two-stage framework that selects task-relevant LLM agents and lets them collaborate through dynamic temporal feed-forward communication networks.
nodes.title: A Dynamic LLM-Powered Agent Network for Task-Oriented Agent Collaboration

nodes.summary: Studies how grounded compositional communication can emerge among cooperative agents trained end-to-end in a physical multi-agent environment without human language supervision.
nodes.title: Emergence of Grounded Compositional Language in Multi-Agent Populations

nodes.summary: Surveys deep-learning-era emergent communication research, framing how deep agents develop task-grounded protocols, how to analyze those protocols, and what remains hard about aligning them with human language.
nodes.title: Emergent Multi-Agent Communication in the Deep Learning Era

nodes.summary: Shows that scaled multi-agent self-play in a physically grounded hide-and-seek environment can induce an autocurriculum of emergent coordination and tool-use strategies without explicit tool-use rewards.
nodes.title: Emergent Tool Use from Multi-Agent Autocurricula

nodes.summary: Defines Degeneration-of-Thought in iterative self-reflection and proposes Multi-Agent Debate, using opposing LLM debaters plus a judge to improve divergent reasoning on commonsense translation and counter-intuitive arithmetic tasks.
nodes.title: Encouraging Divergent Thinking in Large Language Models through Multi-Agent Debate

nodes.summary: Introduces GAIA, a curated real-world benchmark of factoid assistant tasks requiring reasoning, web browsing, multimodal input handling, file reading, coding, and tool use.
nodes.title: GAIA: A Benchmark for General AI Assistants

nodes.summary: Introduces a graph-based framework for composing language agents into swarms and optimizing both node prompts and inter-agent edges across reasoning, coding, puzzle, and tool-use benchmarks.
nodes.title: GPTSwarm: Language Agents as Optimizable Graphs

nodes.summary: Introduces G-Safeguard, a topology-aware defense for LLM-based multi-agent systems that models agent conversations as utterance graphs, detects compromised agents with a GNN, and remediates attacks by pruning risky communication edges.
nodes.title: G-Safeguard: A Topology-Guided Security Lens and Treatment on LLM-based Multi-agent Systems

nodes.summary: Introduces generative agents, an LLM-based architecture for believable interactive agents that use memory retrieval, reflection, and planning to sustain individual and emergent social behavior in a sandbox world.
nodes.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior

nodes.summary: Introduces InternAgent, a closed-loop multi-agent system for moving from research ideas through methodology, code implementation, experiment execution, and verification across 12 AI and science tasks.
nodes.title: InternAgent: When Agent Becomes the Scientist -- Building Closed-Loop System from Hypothesis to Verification

nodes.summary: Surveys LLM-based multi-agent systems through a taxonomy of interfaces, profiling, communication, capability acquisition, applications, resources, and open challenges.
nodes.title: Large Language Model based Multi-Agents: A Survey of Progress and Challenges

nodes.summary: Introduces MADDPG, a centralized-critic and decentralized-actor method for learning coordinated policies in cooperative, competitive, and mixed multi-agent reinforcement learning environments.
nodes.title: Multi-Agent Actor-Critic for Mixed Cooperative-Competitive Environments

nodes.summary: Shows that carefully configured PPO variants, especially MAPPO, are strong baselines across cooperative MARL benchmarks including MPE, SMAC, Google Research Football, and Hanabi.
nodes.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of PPO in Cooperative Multi-Agent Games

nodes.summary: Proposes MAPoRL, a multi-agent reinforcement post-training paradigm that co-trains LLM agents with verifier-based rewards to improve collaborative debate and transfer collaboration behavior across reasoning and inference tasks.
nodes.title: MAPoRL: Multi-Agent Post-Co-Training for Collaborative Large Language Models with Reinforcement Learning

nodes.summary: Reframes building query-specific LLM-based multi-agent systems as a language generation task and trains MAS-GPT to output executable MAS code from a user query in one model inference.
nodes.title: MAS-GPT: Training LLMs to Build LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems

nodes.summary: Introduces MASLab, a unified research codebase that re-implements and evaluates over 20 LLM-based multi-agent methods under shared inputs, configurations, tools, and evaluation protocols.
nodes.title: MASLab: A Unified and Comprehensive Codebase for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems

nodes.summary: Introduces MIRROR, a multi-agent tool-learning framework that combines pre-execution intra-reflection with memory-based inter-reflection to improve LLM tool use and planning reliability.
nodes.title: MIRROR: Multi-agent Intra- and Inter-Reflection for Optimized Reasoning in Tool Learning

nodes.summary: Introduces Meta MLGym and MLGym-Bench, a Gym-style framework and 13-task benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on open-ended AI research workflows with heterogeneous artifacts and metrics.
nodes.title: MLGym: A New Framework and Benchmark for Advancing AI Research Agents

nodes.summary: MaAS searches a query-conditioned distribution of multi-agent architectures so inference can adapt both capability and cost to each task.
nodes.title: Multi-agent Architecture Search via Agentic Supernet

nodes.summary: Introduces Magentic-One, an open-source AutoGen-based generalist multi-agent system whose ledger-driven Orchestrator coordinates web, file, coding, and terminal agents across GAIA, AssistantBench, and WebArena.
nodes.title: Magentic-One: A Generalist Multi-Agent System for Solving Complex Tasks

nodes.summary: Introduces MemGPT, an OS-inspired LLM agent architecture that manages working, recall, and archival memory through function calls to extend fixed-context models across long conversations and document analysis.
nodes.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems

nodes.summary: MemMA coordinates memory construction, retrieval, and repair with specialized agents and an in-situ probe-and-repair loop for long-horizon conversational memory.
nodes.title: MemMA: Coordinating the Memory Cycle through Multi-Agent Reasoning and In-Situ Self-Evolution

nodes.summary: Introduces MetaGPT, a role-specialized multi-agent software-engineering framework that encodes standard operating procedures, structured message sharing, and execution feedback into LLM-based collaboration.
nodes.title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework

nodes.summary: Introduces Mind2Web, a real-website benchmark for high-level web tasks and a two-stage MindAct baseline for grounding language instructions into browser actions.
nodes.title: Mind2Web: Towards a Generalist Agent for the Web

nodes.summary: Introduces Mixture-of-Agents, a prompt-only layered architecture that improves LLM response quality by having multiple open-source models propose, aggregate, and refine answers across benchmarks such as AlpacaEval 2.0, MT-Bench, and FLASK.
nodes.title: Mixture-of-Agents Enhances Large Language Model Capabilities

nodes.summary: Studies Agent Forest, a simple sampling-and-voting ensemble showing that scaling the number of instantiated LLM agents can improve reasoning and code-generation benchmark performance.
nodes.title: More Agents Is All You Need

nodes.summary: MultiAgentBench introduces the MARBLE benchmark for evaluating LLM-agent collaboration and competition across diverse interactive scenarios with task, milestone, and coordination metrics.
nodes.title: MultiAgentBench: Evaluating the Collaboration and Competition of LLM Agents

nodes.summary: Introduces Puppeteer, a centralized reinforcement-learning orchestrator that dynamically selects LLM agents to improve multi-agent reasoning quality while reducing redundant computation.
nodes.title: Multi-Agent Collaboration via Evolving Orchestration

nodes.summary: Uses visual referential games to show that simple neural sender-receiver agents can invent task-useful discrete communication and explores how environment design and supervised naming can push emergent symbols toward semantic and human-interpretable grounding.
nodes.title: Multi-Agent Cooperation and the Emergence of (Natural) Language

nodes.summary: Introduces sequential social dilemmas as Markov-game models of temporally extended cooperation and defection, showing how independent deep RL agents in Gathering and Wolfpack expose cooperation dynamics hidden by matrix-game abstractions.
nodes.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning in Sequential Social Dilemmas

nodes.summary: Introduces Multi-SWE-bench, a human-validated multilingual issue-resolving benchmark and companion RL data initiative for evaluating coding agents beyond Python.
nodes.title: Multi-SWE-bench: A Multilingual Benchmark for Issue Resolving

nodes.summary: Introduces a prompt-only multi-agent debate procedure in which multiple LLM instances exchange and revise answers to improve reasoning and factuality across math, chess, MMLU, and biography-generation tasks.
nodes.title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate

nodes.summary: Proposes OMAC, a supervised framework for optimizing both agent functionality and collaboration structure in LLM-based multi-agent systems through semantic initialization and contrastive refinement.
nodes.title: OMAC: A Holistic Optimization Framework for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration

nodes.summary: Introduces OSWorld, a VM-based real-computer environment and benchmark for evaluating multimodal agents on open-ended desktop, web, file, and cross-application tasks with execution-based evaluation.
nodes.title: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments

nodes.summary: Introduces OpenAgentSafety, a modular benchmark for evaluating tool-using LLM agents on realistic multi-turn safety tasks spanning real tools, benign and adversarial intents, NPC interactions, and hybrid rule-based plus LLM-judge evaluation.
nodes.title: OpenAgentSafety: A Comprehensive Framework for Evaluating Real-World AI Agent Safety

nodes.summary: Presents OpenHands, an open platform for generalist software-using AI agents with a Docker runtime, event-stream architecture, agent hub, multi-agent delegation, and integrated evaluations across software, web, and assistance benchmarks.
nodes.title: OpenHands: An Open Platform for AI Software Developers as Generalist Agents

nodes.summary: Introduces PaperBench, a benchmark for measuring whether AI agents can replicate contemporary ML research papers from scratch using author-approved rubrics and LLM-based judging.
nodes.title: PaperBench: Evaluating AI's Ability to Replicate AI Research

nodes.summary: Introduces QMIX, a monotonic value-factorization method for centralized training with decentralized execution that learns decentralized greedy policies through a state-conditioned mixing network.
nodes.title: QMIX: Monotonic Value Function Factorisation for Deep Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
nodes.venue: Proceedings of the 35th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2018)

nodes.summary: Introduces RIAL and DIAL for learning communication protocols among cooperative partially observable agents, showing how differentiable inter-agent gradients and parameter sharing can produce discrete protocols in switch-riddle and MNIST communication games.
nodes.title: Learning to Communicate with Deep Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

nodes.summary: Introduces ReAct, a prompting paradigm that interleaves natural-language reasoning traces with environment actions so language-model agents can retrieve information, plan, and act across QA, fact verification, text-game, and web-navigation tasks.
nodes.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

nodes.summary: Introduces SMAC, a StarCraft II micromanagement benchmark and PyMARL framework for evaluating cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning under partial observability and decentralized execution.
nodes.title: The StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge (SMAC)

nodes.summary: Introduces SOTOPIA, an interactive environment and multi-dimensional evaluation framework for testing how language agents pursue social goals in open-ended role-play interactions.
nodes.title: SOTOPIA: Interactive Evaluation for Social Intelligence in Language Agents

nodes.summary: Introduces SWE-RL, a rule-based reward reinforcement learning approach that trains Llama 3 on open-source pull request evolution data for real-world issue resolution and broader reasoning gains.
nodes.title: SWE-RL: Advancing LLM Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning on Open Software Evolution

nodes.summary: Introduces SWE-agent and the agent-computer interface framing, showing that LM-tailored search, editing, and context-management tools improve autonomous software-engineering performance on SWE-bench.
nodes.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering

nodes.summary: Introduces SWE-bench-Live, a continuously updatable issue-resolution benchmark built from recent real GitHub issues with automated Docker environment construction and validation.
nodes.title: SWE-bench Goes Live!

nodes.summary: Introduces SWE-bench, a real-world GitHub issue resolution benchmark that evaluates language models by applying generated repository patches and running project tests.
nodes.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?

nodes.summary: Introduces SWE-smith, an environment-first pipeline for synthesizing test-validated software engineering tasks from Python repositories and using them to train open-weight SWE agents.
nodes.title: SWE-smith: Scaling Data for Software Engineering Agents

nodes.summary: Introduces SafeArena, a paired safe/harmful web-agent benchmark for measuring whether autonomous web agents refuse or execute malicious instructions across realistic browser environments.
nodes.title: SafeArena: Evaluating the Safety of Autonomous Web Agents

nodes.summary: Introduces MACNET, a graph-structured framework for scaling LLM-based multi-agent collaboration, and studies how topology, memory control, and agent count affect inference-time collective reasoning.
nodes.title: Scaling Large-Language-Model-based Multi-Agent Collaboration

nodes.summary: Controlled experiments across agent benchmarks show that multi-agent gains depend on task structure, model capability, and coordination overhead rather than agent count alone.
nodes.title: Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems

nodes.summary: Under matched reasoning-token budgets, single-agent LLM systems generally match or outperform multi-agent variants on multi-hop reasoning, except when effective context use is degraded.
nodes.title: Single-Agent LLMs Outperform Multi-Agent Systems on Multi-Hop Reasoning Under Equal Thinking Token Budgets

nodes.summary: SlopCodeBench shows that coding agents can pass local tests while their own carried-forward code becomes progressively more verbose and structurally eroded over iterative tasks.
nodes.title: SlopCodeBench: Benchmarking How Coding Agents Degrade Over Long-Horizon Iterative Tasks

nodes.summary: Introduces TarMAC, a centralized-training/decentralized-execution MARL architecture where agents learn targeted continuous communication and multi-round message passing from task reward.
nodes.title: TarMAC: Targeted Multi-Agent Communication
nodes.venue: Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2019)

nodes.summary: Introduces HPTSA, a hierarchical team of LLM agents for exploiting sandboxed real-world zero-day web vulnerabilities, and reports stronger results than single-agent and scanner baselines on a 14-CVE benchmark.
nodes.title: Teams of LLM Agents can Exploit Zero-Day Vulnerabilities

nodes.summary: Introduces a self-hosted simulated software-company benchmark of 175 workplace tasks for evaluating LLM agents across web, terminal, coding, document, and colleague-interaction workflows.
nodes.title: TheAgentCompany: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Consequential Real World Tasks

nodes.summary: Introduces M500, M1-32B, and a CEO-guided AgentVerse setup for adaptive test-time scaling of multi-agent collaborative reasoning across science QA, math, and coding benchmarks.
nodes.title: Two Heads are Better Than One: Test-time Scaling of Multi-agent Collaborative Reasoning

nodes.summary: Introduces VDN, an additive value-factorization method that learns decentralized agent value functions from a single team reward in cooperative partially observable MARL.
nodes.title: Value-Decomposition Networks For Cooperative Multi-Agent Learning

nodes.summary: Introduces VisualWebArena, a self-hosted benchmark of visually grounded web tasks for evaluating multimodal agents on realistic browser interactions.
nodes.title: VisualWebArena: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Realistic Visually Grounded Web Tasks

nodes.summary: Introduces WarAgent, an LLM-based multi-agent simulation framework for modeling historical international conflicts and probing war triggers through anonymized counterfactual scenarios.
nodes.title: War and Peace (WarAgent): LLM-based Multi-Agent Simulation of World Wars

nodes.summary: Introduces WebArena, a self-hosted realistic web environment and benchmark for evaluating autonomous agents on long-horizon browser tasks with functional correctness checks.
nodes.title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents

nodes.summary: Introduces WebVoyager, a GPT-4V-based multimodal browser agent and real-website benchmark for end-to-end web task completion and trajectory evaluation.
nodes.title: WebVoyager: Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models

nodes.summary: The paper introduces MAST and MAST-Data to classify multi-agent LLM failures across system design, inter-agent misalignment, and task verification.
nodes.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?

nodes.summary: Introduces WorkArena, a ServiceNow-based enterprise web-agent benchmark, and BrowserGym, showing that current LLM browser agents remain far from reliable automation on common knowledge-work tasks.
nodes.title: WorkArena: How Capable are Web Agents at Solving Common Knowledge Work Tasks?

nodes.summary: Introduces a benchmark for evaluating language agents that must converse with simulated users, call domain APIs, follow domain policies, and behave reliably across repeated trials.
nodes.title: tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
